title: Micro-prefetch mesh SDK ergonomics playbook
summary: Working playbook for a lightweight client SDK pattern that coordinates small, network-friendly prefetches across a mesh of hosted API toollets, while preserving typed structured output and clear fallback semantics for streaming responses.
background: We have many SDK and protocol PRDs focused on large-batch prefetch or heavy client-side caching; this doc scopes a different surface: tiny, opportunistic prefetches that 1) reduce median tail latency for common paths, 2) keep incremental streaming semantics intact, and 3) let tool-calls remain typed and replay-safe. It synthesizes ideas from incremental-prefetch, thin-client patterns, and tool-handshake heuristics into a compact SDK ergonomics proposal intended for low-bandwidth and mobile-first clients.
problem_statement: Hosts and mobile clients experience variable network windows and often pay the latency tax for the first tool invocation or schema-resolve step. Current heavy prefetch strategies either increase CPU/memory on client or overfetch irrelevant artifacts. We need an SDK pattern that does narrowly targeted prefetches (micro-prefetch), coordinates them across concurrent sessions (mesh), and surfaces typed tool outcomes without breaking streaming behavior or increasing failure blast radius.
goals: Reduce median first-tool invocation latency by 20-40% for mobile/edge clients on typical conversational flows
Preserve streaming incremental output so UI updates appear as tokens/frames arrive
Ensure tool calls remain typed and idempotent so servers can validate and replay without divergence
Keep SDK surface minimal: 3–4 primitives developers actually use
Fail safely: micro-prefetch must be optional and non-blocking to response delivery
constraints: Must not require server-side changes for any customer not opting into the feature (opt-in default)
Prefetch budget should be bounded by token/byte quota to avoid surprising billing effects
No persistent background processes beyond short-lived network probes on mobile platforms
All typed tool contracts must validate against existing schema versioning rules (no silent schema mutation)
user_scenarios: Mobile chat app: user taps a suggested action; SDK has prefetched the tool schema and a small warm cache of likely args, reducing tool execution round-trip
Editor plugin: lightweight incremental code-run toollets are prefetched so the first lint/run returns earlier while the main generation stream continues
Customer web app on flaky cellular: SDK uses small prefetch lanes over the mesh to attempt schema resolution once and reuse for subsequent sessions
proposed_sdk_surface: Expose a tiny API: (1) prefetchManifest(manifest, priority) — submits a compact set of tool schema ids + hints; (2) declareTool(ToolDescriptor) — lightweight local registration with typed contract; (3) streamCall(request, options) — normal streaming generation that can use prefetched artifacts if available; (4) prefetchStatus(manifestId) — non-blocking inquiry. The manifest shape is intentionally tiny (ids, argument-shape-hints, soft-priority). Default is 'best-effort' and non-blocking. SDKs should expose hooks for telemetry and backpressure hints but must not force synchronous awaits for UI code paths.
streaming_model_behavior: When a streamCall begins, runtime will immediately surface tokens from model generation. If a matching prefetched manifest is present and validated, the runtime will opportunistically attach typed-tool hints inline as 'meta frames' in the incremental stream (compact JSONL frames). If the prefetched manifest is stale, the runtime will fallback to a synchronous tool schema resolve step that is isolated from token emission (i.e., model tokens continue). Meta frames must be idempotent and annotated with a monotonic 'manifest-version' to help clients reconcile partial application.
tool_call_contract: Tool descriptors are typed objects: {tool_id, schema_version, arg_shape_hash, capability_tags}. The server will accept tool invocations if tool_id+schema_version match a registered server-side tool or a compatible fallback. SDK prefetch includes arg_shape_hash to let runtime compute small validation checks locally and avoid obvious mismatches. Tool calls must include a transaction id; if a tool call fails due to schema mismatch, the platform returns a typed 'schema-mismatch' frame and an adaptive suggestion (preferred arg shape) as part of the stream rather than a plain error page.
error_and_fallback_modes: Four graded fallbacks: (1) No-prefetch: normal synchronous schema resolve and tool-call—no interruption to token stream. (2) Partial-prefetch: partial manifest available, use local validation then on-demand fetch for missing bits. (3) Prefetch-mismatch: emit schema-mismatch frame and fallback to synchronous resolve but continue streaming. (4) Circuit-breaker: too many prefetch failures in short window disables micro-prefetch for that client session. All fallbacks must be observable in telemetry and exposed to devs via prefetchStatus hooks.
observability_and_metrics: Minimum metrics: prefetch_attempts, prefetch_success_rate, avg_prefetch_latency, first_tool_latency_with_prefetch, first_tool_latency_without_prefetch, prefetched_manifest_staleness_rate, schema_mismatch_rate. SDK should emit sampled traces for prefetch->tool-call chains with context ids. Provide a small debugging verb that developers can toggle locally to see 'manifest binds' and 'meta-frames' in plain text.
rollout_and_migration_plan: Phase 0: internal alpha — SDKs instrumented in internal apps, opt-in flag only; collect telemetry; duration 4 weeks
Phase 1: limited beta with 5 customers and mobile clients; add server-side lightweight compat layer to accept manifest hints; duration 8 weeks
Phase 2: public opt-in release in SDKs with default off; documentation and migration guide published; duration 6 weeks
Phase 3: evaluate default-on for edge-optimized tiers if telemetry shows stable gains and low failure rates
compatibility_notes: Prefetch manifests are additive hints — servers must ignore unknown manifest fields. Clients should sign manifests with per-session nonces to prevent accidental reuse across unrelated sessions. Maintain strict semantics for schema_version; server-side compatibility rules unchanged. SDKs for older clients should degrade to no-prefetch behavior.
open_questions: Should manifests be billed as normal API calls or treated as a separate, cheaper prefetch quota?
How aggressive should the mesh coordination be when multiple sessions from the same device request overlapping manifests? Coalesce at device-level or session-level?
What limits to impose on manifest size to balance effectiveness vs mobile data usage?
Do we allow server-initiated manifest pushes for long-lived sessions (i.e., server tells client what to prefetch)?
author_notes: This is intentionally compact; target audience is SDK engineers and product PMs who will own the migration. Next steps: prototype Android/iOS minimal prefetch layer, run microbenchmarks on 3 representative networks, and draft a small developer-facing playground that shows meta-frames and typed-tool fallbacks in real time. If reviewers agree, I'll schedule a cross-team sync with serving-runtime and infra to validate cost model assumptions.
